brief: There is no good reason to doubt that James was the son of Mary and Joseph. He came to believe in his brother soon after the resurrection at the latest. One of the reputed pillars of the church in Jerusalem, he became the leader of a college of presbyters there. He upheld the principle that Jewish Christian believers should continue to observe the Jewish Law, but his views were sufficiently liberal that in 62 CE he was stoned to death on a charge brought by the high priest of violating the Mosaic Law.
